openings.claim: Rim-mounted lateral stops might restrain the hatch without making slide resistance depend on squeezing its seal.
openings.delta: Attack hatch-pressure dependence: reconfigure the two padded strip pairs to grip only accessible rim surfaces, with upper strip edges abutting opposite hatch edges along the pull direction. Drill or trim only strips. Withdraw assemblies fully for opening; tether assemblies and pads with cord.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival G0049:R1 obtains restraint through hatch compression. If stop engagement survives the right-contact card disturbance, the replacement should stay within 1 mm under 20 N through ten cycles with reopening within 30 seconds and no new seal tears. It could succeed at negligible hatch preload where the rival slides or lifts a corner. These outcomes are unmeasured.
openings.probe: First establish rim access, edge engagement across the disturbed hatch height, and a reversible conversion between configurations using the same supplies. Reject before fabrication if geometry fails. Complete both configurations within ninety minutes. Allocate twelve trials within twenty observation minutes: two incumbent diagnostic pulls, one disturbed, followed by ten numbered replacement cycles with final disturbance. Record position, corner lift, reopening time and seal condition. Compare the two diagnostic conditions without claiming ten-cycle incumbent validation. Reject on seal tears or permanent fixture deformation.
assumptions: Unspecified rim geometry permits independent strip anchoring and opposing stop contact; no added bracket or adhesive is assumed.
Strip stiffness and rim-clamp friction withstand 20 N without anchor slip or deformation; relocation does not eliminate this capacity dependency.
The card does not lift the hatch beyond stop engagement. Cord length, clearance and manual release permit recoverability and unobstructed opening.
Failure to prepare both configurations or complete twelve informative trials within supplied time defeats this comparison.

assessment: A geometry-and-capacity probe, not deployment. Independent rim anchoring remains indispensable and unknown; no feasible branch is established if it fails.

lineage.reason: Move slide restraint from hatch compression to edge contact while retaining removable strip anchoring.

attacks.dependency: Adequate hatch friction requires pressure that may lift the opposite corner.
